idiom_name: hand-written fixed-slot free list over malloc()/free() with an explicit reset function
implementation_notes: C has no constructors or destructors and no standard-library pool, so the classic structure is written by hand: an array of pre-allocated fixed-size slots plus a free list of pointers, an acquire that pops a slot (or calls the allocation function when the pool may grow), a release that pushes it back, and a reset function the pool calls on every checkout because C will not re-initialise storage for you. Wrap the free list in a pthread_mutex (or a lock-free stack) as soon as more than one thread may acquire. APR's memory pools - apr_pool_create/apr_palloc/apr_pool_clear/apr_pool_destroy - are the nearest library facility, but they recycle whole arenas at clear/destroy boundaries rather than returning instances on release, so instance-level reuse stays manual.
pitfalls: Fixed slot size: one pool serves one size/alignment class, so objects of different sizes need separate pools or the largest size wastes memory in every slot.
No destructor means no automatic cleanup: forgetting the reset call after acquire reproduces the cesspool bug, and a double release corrupts the free list (add a debug 'in pool' flag).
A free-list pool that only grows is indistinguishable from a leak - keep a hard cap and an idle-reclaim path, and free the whole backing array on shutdown.
